title: C4093 — Right rear height sensor connector
introduction:
I start this reference with the right-rear description, then use the connector drawing to reach the circuit table. The housing gives you the outline; the circuit labels give the connections their identities. A recognizable plug shape is only the cover of this little suspension address book.

Find the harness heading, read the drawing’s printed cavity labels, and match each label to the Cavity column. Follow that row across to connect its circuit number, wire description, function and terminal entry. The Function column distinguishes the rear-right suspension-position connection from the control-module connections carrying opposite polarity signs. Use the pigtail table afterward as a separate parts reference.

The page supports identification and circuit-map reading. It does not establish physical access, the connector’s viewing side, test conditions or replacement methods. Gauge conventions and the meanings of Box, Size and Used codes remain undefined here; none should be converted into wire-selection advice, tool dimensions or a diagnosis.

edits.why: The housing detail sits above the horizontal cavity row in the supplied drawing. I use that layout to locate the printed labels, whose order should be read directly rather than assumed to increase from left to right. These are landmarks within the illustration, not proof of a physical viewing direction. The table beneath the image associates it with its Fpn and harness entry.

Cavity is the bridge from drawing to table. Reading across its row keeps Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Terminal Part Number associated. Retain the right-side designation and the positive or negative sign with each control-module description. Those signs identify the listed circuits; they do not authorize a power connection or establish a test value. The blank Qualifier cells add no further configuration detail.

Keep each kit Number together with the Service Part, Image filename and Engineering Shell on its own row. The table records alternatives without explaining how to select between them or install one. Its Gauge entries belong to the pigtail records and should not overwrite the separate circuit-table entries. Matching a shell label alone does not establish interchangeability.
